[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: DM permissions: the core check is in, but I'm still tracing an edge case where an agent gets added to a group DM after it's already started.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] alex: For that group DM edge case, what does the user see if the agent is added late? Does it get history or start blank? Asking for the onboarding copy.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: Right now it starts blank. History backfill is the part I'm tracing, since it touches the same permission check as the other DM cases.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: Policy for the permission check, so we're all building against the same rule: agents never read a DM unless a participant forwards it. That covers late-added agents too, so blank start is correct, no backfill.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] alex: Got it, I'll write the late-add copy around a blank start. Should the agent post a short note saying it can't see earlier messages?
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: A note works, but keep it generic. It shouldn't hint at what was said earlier, only that the agent joined late.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] oli: Double-posting: repro'd it again locally. Looks like two agents both answering the same unaddressed message in a channel. Ticket's up, digging into the runtime dedupe.

[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] nadia: Morning all. Want to line up the release and the paper this week. Who has the latest on contamination fixes and where compute stands?
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: I've got the contamination scan mostly done. A handful of tasks overlap with public repos, still checking licenses on the replacements before I post the list.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: On compute, the last full sweep ran clean overnight. I can slot the rerun once marcus's replacement list is settled.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: Quick check before I lock the pass criteria section: is the harbor workshop paper submission deadline Oct 23? React 👍 if so.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] (nadia reacted 👍)
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Baselines table is still on the old task set. I'll regenerate once the replacements land, otherwise the numbers won't line up with the new items.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Two of the overlapping tasks are near-verbatim from a popular CLI repo. Leaning toward dropping those outright rather than rewriting them, since the solutions are easy to find.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] felix: Release note for planning: the harbor release version is v1.2. It'll carry the contamination replacements once marcus's list is final, so the changelog stays in one place.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If marcus drops those two CLI tasks, I'll check the difficulty spread afterward. Don't want the replacements skewing easy and inflating pass rates.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Good point on difficulty. The replacement candidates I've pulled so far are mostly single-file fixes, so they'd probably skew easy. I'll look for some multi-file ones.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] nadia: Separate thing: we still need someone to own the eval compute reservation for the rerun. Who's taking that on?
---
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Fair warning, the eval jobs have more retries than I do at the gym. Rust timeouts are gonna be the worst offenders.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: I'll also check whether the Rust build tool's test suite pulls anything from the network. If it does, the sandbox will fail those no matter what the model writes.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If it does pull from the network, vendoring the dependencies into the image would fix that. Otherwise we'd have to drop those tasks and look for others.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Vendoring works for me. I can bake the crates into the sandbox image so builds run offline. Marcus, send me the lockfile once you pick the tasks.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Will do. Checking now whether the lockfile is pinned for that Rust tool. If it isn't, I'll resolve versions first so the crates don't drift.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If the lockfile isn't pinned, note which crate versions you resolve to. I'd like the paper's appendix to list the toolchain so the Rust tasks are reproducible.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Lockfile's checked in but a couple of entries use loose version ranges. I'll resolve them and write down what each crate lands on.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Once the crates are resolved I'll bake them into a test image and do a dry run on the Rust tasks, just to see where the slow ones land.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: When you do the dry run, log per-task wall time too. I'd like to see whether the slow Rust tasks cluster on the multi-file ones.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Per-task wall time would also help the baseline table. I can add a column for median runtime per language if the logs have it.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] felix: Per-task wall time is already in the harness logs, I'll make sure it gets exported with the results so Theo's runtime column doesn't need scraping.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Two of the Rust candidates look like they share a fixture directory, so I'll check they don't leak each other's expected outputs before they go in.
---
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] nadia: Ok, we need to nail down the release gate and what goes in the held-out set today. Marcus, where are we on licensing for the scraped repos?
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Mostly sorted. Most repos are MIT or Apache, but a handful have no license file at all, so I'm leaning toward dropping those until we hear back from maintainers.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Dropping the unlicensed ones makes sense to me. Do we know if they skew toward any particular task type? Don't want the held-out set lopsided afterward.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Checking now. Gut feeling is the unlicensed ones cluster in small CLI tools and research code, so refactoring and bug-fix tasks might take the hit.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Ok, that matters for the gate then. Release gate threshold is 70% pass@1, so if the bug-fix slice shrinks a lot we should check the variance on it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: I can rerun the bug-fix slice with a few seeds on the current baseline to see how noisy it is once those repos are out.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: also, that number is measured on the held-out set only, not dev. Dev scores shouldn't count toward it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Bug-fix looks like the worst hit. A lot of the unlicensed ones are single-file scripts with small, self-contained failing tests, which are the cleanest bug-fix items.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Decision for the held-out set: it's 1,200 items, locked in after the unlicensed repos come out. If bug-fix ends up too thin, I'll backfill from licensed repos rather than shrink the total.

[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] nadia: Ok, we need to nail down the release gate and what goes in the held-out set today. Marcus, where are we on licensing for the scraped repos?
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Mostly sorted. Most repos are MIT or Apache, but a handful have no license file at all, so I'm leaning toward dropping those until we hear back from maintainers.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Dropping the unlicensed ones makes sense to me. Do we know if they skew toward any particular task type? Don't want the held-out set lopsided afterward.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Checking now. Gut feeling is the unlicensed ones cluster in small CLI tools and research code, so refactoring and bug-fix tasks might take the hit.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Ok, that matters for the gate then. Release gate threshold is 70% pass@1, so if the bug-fix slice shrinks a lot we should check the variance on it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: I can rerun the bug-fix slice with a few seeds on the current baseline to see how noisy it is once those repos are out.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: also, that number is measured on the held-out set only, not dev. Dev scores shouldn't count toward it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Bug-fix looks like the worst hit. A lot of the unlicensed ones are single-file scripts with small, self-contained failing tests, which are the cleanest bug-fix items.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Decision for the held-out set: it's 1,200 items, locked in after the unlicensed repos come out. If bug-fix ends up too thin, I'll backfill from licensed repos rather than shrink the total.

[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] elena: Checked timeouts. The multi-file repos need a longer setup window for dependency installs, otherwise some items will fail before the tests even start.

memory_text:
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] nadia: Ok, we need to nail down the release gate and what goes in the held-out set today. Marcus, where are we on licensing for the scraped repos?
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Mostly sorted. Most repos are MIT or Apache, but a handful have no license file at all, so I'm leaning toward dropping those until we hear back from maintainers.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Dropping the unlicensed ones makes sense to me. Do we know if they skew toward any particular task type? Don't want the held-out set lopsided afterward.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Checking now. Gut feeling is the unlicensed ones cluster in small CLI tools and research code, so refactoring and bug-fix tasks might take the hit.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Ok, that matters for the gate then. Release gate threshold is 70% pass@1, so if the bug-fix slice shrinks a lot we should check the variance on it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: I can rerun the bug-fix slice with a few seeds on the current baseline to see how noisy it is once those repos are out.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: also, that number is measured on the held-out set only, not dev. Dev scores shouldn't count toward it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Bug-fix looks like the worst hit. A lot of the unlicensed ones are single-file scripts with small, self-contained failing tests, which are the cleanest bug-fix items.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Decision for the held-out set: it's 1,200 items, locked in after the unlicensed repos come out. If bug-fix ends up too thin, I'll backfill from licensed repos rather than shrink the total.
---
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] nadia: For the paper, let's call that bucket "environment failures" rather than model errors. Reviewers will read it more kindly, and it's more accurate.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Fine by me. Should we report environment failures as a separate rate per slice, so readers see how much each slice is affected?
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: Yes, per-slice rate works. I'll add it to the results table. Also, I put in the draft that the release gate is 75% pass@1, so the environment-failure rate sits right next to it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: nice, that matches what I saw on my branch. once the patch works, add a test with a hyphenated pool name so it doesn't regress.
---
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Fair warning, the eval jobs have more retries than I do at the gym. Rust timeouts are gonna be the worst offenders.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: I'll also check whether the Rust build tool's test suite pulls anything from the network. If it does, the sandbox will fail those no matter what the model writes.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If it does pull from the network, vendoring the dependencies into the image would fix that. Otherwise we'd have to drop those tasks and look for others.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Vendoring works for me. I can bake the crates into the sandbox image so builds run offline. Marcus, send me the lockfile once you pick the tasks.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Will do. Checking now whether the lockfile is pinned for that Rust tool. If it isn't, I'll resolve versions first so the crates don't drift.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If the lockfile isn't pinned, note which crate versions you resolve to. I'd like the paper's appendix to list the toolchain so the Rust tasks are reproducible.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Lockfile's checked in but a couple of entries use loose version ranges. I'll resolve them and write down what each crate lands on.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Once the crates are resolved I'll bake them into a test image and do a dry run on the Rust tasks, just to see where the slow ones land.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: When you do the dry run, log per-task wall time too. I'd like to see whether the slow Rust tasks cluster on the multi-file ones.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Per-task wall time would also help the baseline table. I can add a column for median runtime per language if the logs have it.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] felix: Per-task wall time is already in the harness logs, I'll make sure it gets exported with the results so Theo's runtime column doesn't need scraping.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Two of the Rust candidates look like they share a fixture directory, so I'll check they don't leak each other's expected outputs before they go in.

label: IGNORE
reason: No fact I can point to contradicts the 1,200 item count (the Oct 19 draft also says 1,200), and Elena's rerun tomorrow is a vague personal plan that I don't need to track.
memory_text:
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] felix: Going with what I proposed last Wednesday (Oct 7) for the new harbor release. Starting on it now, will rebuild the candidate as soon as Marcus's flagged list lands.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] theo: Do I rerun every baseline from scratch, or just rescore the surviving tasks from the saved traces? Rescoring would be way faster for the slow scaffolds.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] yuki: Rescoring is fine for tasks whose test harness didn't change. Any task we patch to drop near-duplicate overlap needs a fresh run, though.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] marcus: Near-duplicate check is doable. I'll run fuzzy matching on the solution diffs against the fork and gist dumps, then flag anything above a similarity cutoff.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] yuki: Updating the eval config now to point at v1.3. Patched tasks get fresh runs, the rest can reuse saved traces. I'll flag which is which in the config.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] elena: For the fresh runs, which scaffolds are slowest? I'd like to queue those first so they don't get stuck behind the quick ones.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] theo: The multi-file refactor scaffolds are slowest by far, especially the one with the long tool-use loops. Those should go first in the queue.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] elena: Got it, I'll put the refactor ones at the front. The long tool-use loops tend to hit timeouts, so I'll bump the per-run limit for those.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] theo: Heads up, the long tool-use scaffold also eats a lot of tokens per run, so the logs get huge. Might want to check disk before queueing.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] elena: Good call on disk. I'll check free space on the shared volume and point the big logs at scratch before queueing anything.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] marcus: Fuzzy match on the fork dumps is running. A few gist hits look like reformatted copies, so whitespace and renamed variables won't fool it.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] theo: Ok, committing: I'll rerun all baselines on harbor v1.3 and have them done by Fri Oct 16. Rescoring the unpatched tasks from saved traces, fresh runs only for the patched ones.
---
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] marcus: For the paper, we should describe the near-duplicate similarity cutoff in the contamination section. Reviewers will ask how we picked it.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] yuki: Agreed. A histogram of similarity scores would help, if there's a visible gap between reformatted copies and legit lookalikes, the cutoff justifies itself.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] theo: Rescored runs on the untouched tasks look nearly identical so far. Curious if the patched ones drop more on the refactor scaffolds.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] theo: Quick one, who actually holds the compute reservation for the fresh runs? Want to make sure the refactor jobs land on it.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] elena: That's me, I hold the reservation. Refactor jobs are already at the front of the queue, so they'll land on it.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] marcus: Histogram's rough but promising: reformatted gist copies bunch up at the top, and generic argparse-style boilerplate lookalikes sit well below with a clear dip between.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] yuki: That dip is exactly what we want. Can you overlay the borderline cases on the histogram? I'd like to see where the ambiguous ones fall.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] marcus: Sure, I'll mark the borderline ones in a different color. A few are fixtures copied from a popular tutorial repo, so they might land near the dip.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] yuki: Tutorial-repo fixtures are a good edge case. If they sit near the dip, I'd say describe them separately in the paper rather than force them into either bucket.
---
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] yuki: Recorded runs works for me. We could replay a few agent traces on a projector and talk through them, honestly more useful than live.
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] yuki: Once the ids are in, can you also log which categories each removal came from? I'd like that next to the plateau figure.
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] theo: Got it, I'll add a category column to the export so the removal counts sit beside the per-category pass rates. Plateau figure should line up then.
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] felix: Good, I'll find traces where the agent loops on a flaky test. Those make better discussion than clean passes. Lake house is looking good.
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] elena: If the tables regenerate, do the plateau curves need a rerun too, or are those computed from cached trajectories?
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] theo: Curves come from cached trajectories, so no rerun. Just refilter by id and regenerate. Only the plateau figure needs a fresh pass with the smaller denominator.
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] yuki: Before the refilter, can someone check the build-loop task I picked for the transcript isn't among the removed ids? Awkward to show a task we dropped.
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] marcus: Good catch. That build-loop task is a CLI tooling repo, not a web-app fork, so it's likely fine. I'll grep the id file against it to be sure.
[Mon Oct 19 #harbor-evals] theo: Dataset section in the draft says 1,200 items, so I'm building the tables to match that. Will grep the plateau task id once Marcus's file is up.

[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] rachel: Kicking off the Northwind renewal thread. Want one place for timeline, pricing, sponsor, and paperwork. Keiko, any early signals from their side?
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] keiko: Yes, a couple. Their clinical informatics lead mentioned on our last call that usage has grown a lot since the pilot teams went live. Sounds happy overall.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] gabe: Good sign. Growth like that usually means we should check their rate limit headroom before we talk renewal. Want me to pull usage trends?
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] rachel: Yes please, Gabe. Timeline note for everyone: the Northwind renewal signature deadline is Oct 30. Working back from that for pricing, legal review, and sponsor sign-off.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] gabe: On it. I'll also check whether any of their pilot teams are bursting at peak hours, since that's usually where throttling shows up first.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] tomas: Once Gabe's usage numbers are in, I'll draft the pricing options for the order form. Rachel, any sense of how aggressive they'll be on discount?
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] rachel: Honestly not sure yet. Their procurement team pushed hard last cycle, so I'd expect them to open with a big ask.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] rachel: Tomas, quick check before we plan the negotiation: is the Northwind discount currently 18% off list? Want to confirm before I anchor anything with them.

[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] dmitri: Kickoff thread for kestrel. Need start date, allocation, stability rules and data readiness all pinned down in here today. Who has blockers?

[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: Do those flapping leaf switches sit in the pod I was planning to hand kestrel? If so I need to rework the allocation table.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Yes, same pod. Both flapping leafs feed racks in that pod. Seeing CRC errors on the uplinks, so I'm leaning optics, but not confirmed.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] dmitri: Decision: kestrel starts Oct 5. Lucia, get the optics vs firmware call made and fixed well before then. Wen, redo the allocation table around whatever the pod looks like once that's resolved.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Pulling optic transceiver serials on the flapping uplinks now. If they share a batch, that settles it. Will swap one and rerun all-reduce soak.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: Whichever way the optics call goes, I'll draft two allocation variants: one with the flapping racks drained, one assuming they come back clean.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] dmitri: Quick check Wen: is the kestrel node allocation 2,048 nodes? Want that confirmed before the variants go out.
---
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Lucia, can you send me the port-to-rank mapping for the flapping uplinks? I want straggler alerts to tag those ranks directly.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Yep, mapping coming. Both ports sit on the same leaf switch, so it's a handful of ranks per node. Exporting from the switch config now.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Thanks. Once I have it I'll also add per-rank NCCL timing to the dashboard, so a slow allreduce on those ranks is visible right away.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Lucia, when the other uplink gets swapped, give me a heads-up. If those racks drop mid-soak I want to see how the staging path handles a rank vanishing.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Will do. Swapping the second optic after the current soak window closes, so CRC counters on the first port stay a clean baseline.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Heads up, the cluster room is louder than a jet engine today. Swapping optics in there with earplugs in, so slow to reply if I miss pings.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Once the mapping lands I'll also check whether those ranks end up in the same NCCL ring segment. A flaky one could stall the whole ring.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: If the ring segment does include those ranks, I can reshuffle placement so they land on a different leaf. Cheap on my side.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Mapping would also let me flag whether those ranks show up as stragglers in the last burn-in logs. Pulling those now to compare.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] dmitri: If those ranks show up as stragglers in burn-in, I want that in the writeup before we lock the placement.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: Pulling the current placement map now so I can see which leaf those ranks sit on and what's free to swap into.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Mapping exported. Both ports are on leaf 7, and the ranks are mostly the last GPU slots per node. Dropping the CSV in the channel.
---
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: yep, confirmed
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: If the flapping racks get drained, I need to know before I size checkpoint shards. Fewer nodes changes the per-rank write pattern to storage.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Data side is looking fine so far. Tokenized shards are landing on the new filesystem, just waiting on the last dedup pass to finish.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Whichever variant wins, I want straggler detection on from step zero. Flapping links would show up as a few slow ranks dragging MFU down.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Stability rule for the run: roll back if loss rises more than 15%. I'll wire that into the monitor alongside the straggler alerts.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Also want async checkpoint staging on local NVMe before flush, otherwise a slow writer rank will stall the whole step. Testing that on the new filesystem.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Also, that's measured over a 200-step window, not single-step spikes, so one noisy batch won't trip it.
---
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Serials back: both flapping uplinks have transceivers from the same vendor lot. Swapped one, soak is running now, watching CRC counters on that port.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: If the swapped port stays clean, I'd want the other flapping uplink swapped too before I count those racks as healthy in the second variant.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Sized the data loader for 2,560 nodes. Filesystem read throughput has headroom, and prefetch workers per node should keep the GPUs fed. Dedup finishing is the only gate on my side.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: NVMe staging test looks good so far: flush overlaps the next forward pass, no stalls on the slow writer. Restore path from the new filesystem still untested.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: CRC counters on the swapped port are flat so far. Other flapping uplink still on the old optic, I'll swap it next and rerun the soak.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] dmitri: Mateo, your loader sizing doesn't match the allocation Wen confirmed. Redo it against the confirmed number.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Fair, my bad. Redoing the loader sizing against Wen's number. Prefetch worker count per node will probably shift too, rechecking read throughput after.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Restore path is my next test. Will kill a rank mid-flush and confirm we resume cleanly from the staged NVMe copy.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Once dedup lands, I'll finish moving the tokenized datasets to the new storage tier by Fri Oct 2. That leaves a few days of buffer before the start.

[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] lucia: Likely correlated. The bump landed on the leaf where the writer nodes uplink. Pulling port counters to see if it was incast on that leaf.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] kofi: If it's incast on that leaf, I can stagger the writer nodes' flush start so they don't all burst at once. Want to see the counters first.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] lucia: Port counters show egress buffer spikes on the writer uplinks right at flush start. Looks like incast. Staggering would probably flatten it.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] kofi: Okay, I'll add a per-node jitter on the flush start so the writers spread out. Hana, watch step time on the next save for any residual dip.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] mateo: Unrelated to the flush, but I'm seeing IB link flaps on a couple of the dataloader nodes in my logs. Who's on call for fabric incidents today?
---
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] dmitri: Morning. Launch day. Post your final go/no-go here before I kick off, and I want eyes on stragglers from step 1.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] lucia: Fabric side looks clean on my end. IB link flap counters are flat since the last sweep, no pending cable tickets.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] wen: Allocation is sitting idle and healthy in the scheduler, no drained nodes flagged. Watching for any that flip to unhealthy during job startup.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] kofi: Checkpoint writer is up on my side. I'll watch async flush times on the first saves, since stalls there tend to show up as stragglers.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] hana: Loss and grad-norm dashboards are live. I'm also tracking per-rank step time so a slow rank shows up before MFU dips.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] mateo: Dataloader workers are warm and prefetch queues look full. Should be smooth on the first few batches, no stalls expected from the data side.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] dmitri: Good. Kicking off now. Shout the second you see a rank lagging, don't wait for it to show up in MFU.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] hana: First steps are in. Per-rank step time looks tight so far, no rank trailing the pack. Still early though.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] wen: Heads up, separate from kestrel: the kestrel-mini ablation run starts Oct 14. Different run, I'll keep its nodes carved out so it doesn't touch this allocation.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] kofi: First async flush is kicking off now. Writer queue depth looks normal, nothing backing up behind the flush yet.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] lucia: Seeing a brief NCCL all-reduce latency bump on one leaf switch during the flush. Still within normal spread, keeping an eye on it.
[Mon Oct 12 #kestrel-run] kofi: Flush finished clean on my side. Lucia, does that latency bump line up with the writer burst hitting the fabric, or is it unrelated?
---
[Wed Sep 30 #infra] lucia: Firmware rollout on the IB leaf switches is staged but not pushed. Seeing a few flapping links on rack group C that I want to look at first.
[Wed Sep 30 #infra] kofi: Are the flapping links on C causing NCCL timeouts yet? Want to know if checkpoint writes from those nodes are getting stalled mid-save.
[Wed Sep 30 #infra] hana: Quick check while we're on checkpoints: kestrel checkpoint cadence is every 500 steps, right? React ✅ if that's what you have.
[Wed Sep 30 #infra] (kofi reacted ✅)
[Wed Sep 30 #infra] lucia: Not seeing NCCL timeouts yet, just symbol errors and retrains on a couple of C uplinks. Checking cable seating before touching firmware.
[Wed Sep 30 #infra] kofi: Good. If those C uplinks retrain mid-save, I'd expect partial shards on the writer ranks. I'll check how the async flush handles a stalled write.
[Wed Sep 30 #infra] wen: Who's owning fabric incident on-call for kestrel right now? I need a name on the rota before I lock the allocation table.
---
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] wen: Vendor folks want to come onsite and look at the cluster. Dmitri, you want to be in the room for that or should I just handle it?
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] wen: Which leaf is that? Want to see if any kestrel nodes hang off it before I touch the spare pool.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] dmitri: I'd like to be there. Want them to see the IB fabric flaps firsthand, not just hear about them secondhand.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] lucia: Leaf 14, uplink on the second spine side. Checking now which node ranks map to it, will paste the list.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] wen: Makes sense. Lucia's flap logs would help here. I'd also like them to check the transceivers on the leaf switches while they're in the hall.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] kofi: Going with my Oct 5 suggestion on the kestrel checkpoint cadence. Applying it now, so the restart drill will exercise it. Hana, I'll check your timeline after.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] hana: Kofi, which suggestion is that? Don't see it in the doc. Need to know what the drill is actually exercising before I set up the monitoring side.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] dmitri: Yes, transceivers too. Flaps cluster on a few leaf ports, so I want vendor eyes on those optics and the cable runs.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] lucia: Leaf 14 maps to a contiguous block of kestrel ranks in one rack. No NCCL timeouts on them so far. List is in the doc.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] wen: Single rack block is easy to drain if it comes to that. Checking which spares sit off leaf 14 so we're not swapping onto the same uplink.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] kofi: My bad, it lives in the ckpt-writer thread, not the doc. It touches the save interval and the async flush path. Pasting it here.
[Fri Oct 9 #infra] hana: Thanks. Once it's pasted I'll check whether the async flush overlaps with the step-time stalls I'm alerting on, otherwise the drill will look noisy.

label: INTERVENE
cited_value: roll back if loss rises more than 15%, measured over a 200-step window
reason: Lucia quotes a rollback threshold of 20% over 300 steps, but Hana's stability rule set in #kestrel-run is 15% over a 200-step window, and she is planning the staging test around the wrong numbers.
memory_text:
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: yep, confirmed
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: If the flapping racks get drained, I need to know before I size checkpoint shards. Fewer nodes changes the per-rank write pattern to storage.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Data side is looking fine so far. Tokenized shards are landing on the new filesystem, just waiting on the last dedup pass to finish.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Whichever variant wins, I want straggler detection on from step zero. Flapping links would show up as a few slow ranks dragging MFU down.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Stability rule for the run: roll back if loss rises more than 15%. I'll wire that into the monitor alongside the straggler alerts.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Also want async checkpoint staging on local NVMe before flush, otherwise a slow writer rank will stall the whole step. Testing that on the new filesystem.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Also, that's measured over a 200-step window, not single-step spikes, so one noisy batch won't trip it.
---
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Serials back: both flapping uplinks have transceivers from the same vendor lot. Swapped one, soak is running now, watching CRC counters on that port.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: If the swapped port stays clean, I'd want the other flapping uplink swapped too before I count those racks as healthy in the second variant.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Sized the data loader for 2,560 nodes. Filesystem read throughput has headroom, and prefetch workers per node should keep the GPUs fed. Dedup finishing is the only gate on my side.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: NVMe staging test looks good so far: flush overlaps the next forward pass, no stalls on the slow writer. Restore path from the new filesystem still untested.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: CRC counters on the swapped port are flat so far. Other flapping uplink still on the old optic, I'll swap it next and rerun the soak.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] dmitri: Mateo, your loader sizing doesn't match the allocation Wen confirmed. Redo it against the confirmed number.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Fair, my bad. Redoing the loader sizing against Wen's number. Prefetch worker count per node will probably shift too, rechecking read throughput after.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Restore path is my next test. Will kill a rank mid-flush and confirm we resume cleanly from the staged NVMe copy.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] mateo: Once dedup lands, I'll finish moving the tokenized datasets to the new storage tier by Fri Oct 2. That leaves a few days of buffer before the start.
---
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Lucia, can you send me the port-to-rank mapping for the flapping uplinks? I want straggler alerts to tag those ranks directly.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Yep, mapping coming. Both ports sit on the same leaf switch, so it's a handful of ranks per node. Exporting from the switch config now.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Thanks. Once I have it I'll also add per-rank NCCL timing to the dashboard, so a slow allreduce on those ranks is visible right away.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Lucia, when the other uplink gets swapped, give me a heads-up. If those racks drop mid-soak I want to see how the staging path handles a rank vanishing.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Will do. Swapping the second optic after the current soak window closes, so CRC counters on the first port stay a clean baseline.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Heads up, the cluster room is louder than a jet engine today. Swapping optics in there with earplugs in, so slow to reply if I miss pings.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: Once the mapping lands I'll also check whether those ranks end up in the same NCCL ring segment. A flaky one could stall the whole ring.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: If the ring segment does include those ranks, I can reshuffle placement so they land on a different leaf. Cheap on my side.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Mapping would also let me flag whether those ranks show up as stragglers in the last burn-in logs. Pulling those now to compare.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] dmitri: If those ranks show up as stragglers in burn-in, I want that in the writeup before we lock the placement.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] wen: Pulling the current placement map now so I can see which leaf those ranks sit on and what's free to swap into.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Mapping exported. Both ports are on leaf 7, and the ranks are mostly the last GPU slots per node. Dropping the CSV in the channel.
---
[topic start] [Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Lucia, can you send me the port-to-rank mapping for the flapping uplinks? I want straggler alerts to tag those ranks directly.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Got the CSV. Cross-referencing against burn-in straggler logs now, last GPU slots on leaf 7 are my first suspects.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] kofi: If the last GPU slots on leaf 7 are the stragglers, I'll add those ranks to my kill-mid-flush test. Curious how staging handles a slow writer there.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] hana: Burn-in logs show leaf 7 last-slot ranks lagging on allreduce in a few windows. Not conclusive yet, still lining up timestamps against the CRC spikes.
[Mon Sep 28 #kestrel-run] lucia: Once timestamps line up, send me the spike windows. If CRC bursts match the lag, I'll pull that leaf 7 optic first.
